result.instructions: Mesh Control Engine editor. One project per process. Scenes are .mcscene documents of entities (id, name, reflected components). Discover component types with refl_list_components / refl_describe_component; read with scene_info, scene_list_entities, scene_get_entity, asset_list; edit with entity_* and component_* (values use the .mcscene spelling: vectors as arrays, assets as "guid:<uuid>", entity references as "$<entity id>", enums by name). Edits stay in memory until scene_save. Verify with cook_run, cook_errors and run_headless (deterministic: same scene + ticks = same state_hash). Docs, samples and examples: mce://docs/index, docs_search; what is data and what needs code: engine_capabilities; prompts start_game, add_level, polish_pass. Something the engine made hard: report_friction.

tools.name: refl_list_components
tools.description: List every reflected component type (name and field count).

tools.name: refl_describe_component
tools.description: Describe a component type, or a reflected value type such as UiAnchors or UiStyle (runtime UI): fields with kind, array count, nested struct fields, enum values, editor range, read-only/transient flags and help text.

tools.name: scene_info
tools.description: The open scene: name, GUID, path under assets/, unsaved changes, entity count.

tools.name: scene_list_entities
tools.description: List the scene's entities in file order: id, name, component types. Optional component filter.

tools.name: scene_get_entity
tools.description: One entity (by id, or by name when unique) with its component values in .mcscene form (fields at their default are omitted; entity references are "$<id>"; a value you write may also name the entity). Ids are saved in the file and survive scene_open.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: asset_list
tools.description: Assets of the project (GUID registry): guid as "guid:<uuid>", path under assets/, type.

type.description: Texture, Font, Sfx, Scene, Mesh, Material, ...

tools.name: asset_set_import_settings
tools.description: Replace an asset's importer settings in its .mceasset sidecar (texture: {"srgb": bool, "mips": bool}; a normal map or LUT needs srgb false). Keys are validated by the next cook_run.

tools.name: entity_create
tools.description: Create an entity (with a LocalTransform unless transform is false) and optionally components, e.g. {"Sprite": {"texture": "guid:...", "size": [1, 1]}}. With 'prefab', an instance of that .mcprefab whose 'components' override the prefab root's fields (LocalTransform places it). An entity reference field takes "$<id>", the entity's unique name, or null. Returns its id.

prefab.description: "guid:<uuid>" of a .mcprefab: place an instance; components then override the prefab root's fields

at.description: Index in the hierarchy; default: the end

tools.name: entity_delete
tools.description: Delete an entity (references to it become null).

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: scene_clear
tools.description: Delete every entity of the open scene (one undo step): re-author a scene keeping its GUID and path.

tools.name: entity_duplicate
tools.description: Duplicate an entity right after itself. Returns the new id(s).

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: component_add
tools.description: Add a component (default values, or patched with 'value': an object of fields).

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: component_remove
tools.description: Remove a component from an entity.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: component_set
tools.description: Change a component. Without 'path', 'value' is an object of fields to change. With a property path ("position", "position.x", "shape.half", "items[2]"), 'value' is that property's value. An entity reference takes "$<id>", the entity's unique name, or null. Type errors name the expected type.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: scene_new
tools.description: Start a new, empty, unsaved scene (refuses to drop unsaved changes unless force).

tools.name: scene_open
tools.description: Open a .mcscene, or a .mcprefab to edit the prefab itself (entity 0 is its root), by its path under assets/ (refuses to drop unsaved changes unless force).

tools.name: scene_save
tools.description: Save the scene (atomic write; entity ids are saved with it). With 'path' (under assets/): save as, with a fresh GUID for a new file. 'name' renames the scene. When another agent saved the file since it was opened, their edits are merged in entity by entity; edits to the same component of an entity conflict and nothing is written unless resolve picks a side. Refuses to overwrite another existing file unless force (an overwritten file keeps its GUID; force skips the merge). A path ending in .mcprefab saves the document as a prefab (entity 0 is the root; prefab_create_from makes one from an entity).

tools.name: scene_undo
tools.description: Undo the last scene edit (one tools/call is one step; editor edits share the history).

tools.name: scene_redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone scene edit.

tools.name: cook_run
tools.description: Cook the project (incremental) into <project>/cooked. pack: also write <project>/assets.mce (a host built from the project plays its own build-tree pack unless started with -pack <that file or the cooked dir>). adopt: give new source files (a PNG, WAV or TTF added under assets/ with no .mceasset sidecar) a sidecar with a fresh GUID instead of a cook error. Returns counts, diagnostics with file:line and the output paths (relative to the project folder).

tools.name: cook_errors
tools.description: Diagnostics of the last cook (file, line, col, stage, message).

tools.name: asset_delete
tools.description: Delete a source file under assets/ together with its .mceasset sidecar (not the open scene). The catalog is rescanned.

tools.name: run_headless
tools.description: Cook, then play the saved scene headless for N fixed ticks exactly as the game's host plays it with -headless (the game's own systems included in a project server), or another saved scene of the project with 'scene'. Returns the World state_hash (same scene + ticks + input = same hash), World metrics and the log tail. input: scripted keyboard/gamepad actions per tick, as the game reads them from InputState ("Move" [x,y], "Jump", "Fire", "Pause", "Confirm", "Cancel" and any game-defined action name); a press is a one-tick segment, a hold a range. inspect: after the last tick, report the live component values (Transient runtime fields included) of scene entities by id and/or of every entity with a component (at most 64); show picks the components to print. trace: component fields of scene entities every N ticks, as series (how a value moved over the run, not only where it ended).

scene.description: Play this saved scene (path under assets/) instead of the open one; inspect then takes 'component' only

input.description: Either a script string, one segment per line: "<from>[-<to>] Action[=value] ..." (e.g. "10-70 Move=1,0 Jump\n100 Fire"), or an array of segments

actions.description: Action name -> true, a number, or [x, y]

component.description: Every live entity with this component (also ones the run spawned)

show.description: Components to print (default: the entity's scene components, or the filter component + LocalTransform)

trace.description: Sample fields during the run: {"every": ticks (10), "fields": [{"entity": id or name, "field": "LocalTransform.position.x"}]} (at most 16 fields, 1000 rows)

tools.name: console_list
tools.description: List console variables (type, value, flags, help) and console functions. Optional name prefix.

tools.name: console_exec
tools.description: Execute one console line ("name" prints, "name value" sets, "func args" calls). Cheat and restart-only variables are refused unless the server runs with --allow-cheats.

tools.name: render_frame
tools.description: See the game: draw the open (saved) or another saved scene with the real player at sim tick N, with scripted input, from its own camera or another, at a chosen size and safe area. Returns the frame as a PNG image. Works without a GPU (offscreen software rendering). 'save' also writes the PNG under the project folder.

tick.description: Capture the first frame after this sim tick

scene.description: Render this saved scene (path under assets/) instead of the open one

input.description: Scripted input as run_headless takes it: a script string ("10-70 Move=1,0 Jump") or an array of {from, to, actions}

camera.description: Render from another camera (render only, the sim is unchanged): {"entity": id or name} of a camera entity in the open scene, {"index": n} (scene entity index), {"position": [x,y,z], "target": [x,y,z], "fov": deg} (free 3D) or {"center": [x,y], "zoom": z} (free 2D)

safe_area.description: Pretend the screen has these safe-area insets in pixels {left, top, right, bottom}: UI lays out inside them and the image outlines them

software.description: Force the offscreen software renderer (automatic when there is no display)

save.description: Also write the frame as a PNG at this path inside the project folder, e.g. shots/title.png

tools.name: render_sheet
tools.description: A contact sheet: frames at several ticks (columns) from one or more cameras (rows) in one image, each cell labelled with its tick. One player run per camera.

cameras.description: Camera objects as render_frame's 'camera'; default: the scene's own

scene.description: Render this saved scene (path under assets/) instead of the open one

input.description: Scripted input as run_headless takes it: a script string ("10-70 Move=1,0 Jump") or an array of {from, to, actions}

camera.description: Render from another camera (render only, the sim is unchanged): {"entity": id or name} of a camera entity in the open scene, {"index": n} (scene entity index), {"position": [x,y,z], "target": [x,y,z], "fov": deg} (free 3D) or {"center": [x,y], "zoom": z} (free 2D)

safe_area.description: Pretend the screen has these safe-area insets in pixels {left, top, right, bottom}: UI lays out inside them and the image outlines them

software.description: Force the offscreen software renderer (automatic when there is no display)

tools.name: image_diff
tools.description: Compare a frame with a golden PNG in the project: 'image' (a PNG in the project) or 'render' (render_frame's arguments). Returns the score (mean channel difference, 0..1), the changed fraction and pass (score <= max_score), with a heat map image. With no golden yet, or update: true, the image becomes the golden.

golden.description: PNG path inside the project folder, e.g. goldens/title.png

image.description: PNG path inside the project folder to compare

render.description: render_frame arguments: the frame to compare

tick.description: Capture the first frame after this sim tick

scene.description: Render this saved scene (path under assets/) instead of the open one

input.description: Scripted input as run_headless takes it: a script string ("10-70 Move=1,0 Jump") or an array of {from, to, actions}

camera.description: Render from another camera (render only, the sim is unchanged): {"entity": id or name} of a camera entity in the open scene, {"index": n} (scene entity index), {"position": [x,y,z], "target": [x,y,z], "fov": deg} (free 3D) or {"center": [x,y], "zoom": z} (free 2D)

safe_area.description: Pretend the screen has these safe-area insets in pixels {left, top, right, bottom}: UI lays out inside them and the image outlines them

software.description: Force the offscreen software renderer (automatic when there is no display)

threshold.description: Channel difference a pixel may have and still count as unchanged

update.description: Write the image as the new golden

tools.name: module_build
tools.description: Rebuild the game module with the project's CMake build (the tree the loaded module came from) and map the new build into this server: new and changed components and systems are live for the next tool call, no restart. Returns the compiler's errors (and with warnings: true its warnings) as {severity, file, line, col, message}, plus the output's end when the build failed. The open scene is kept (re-read with the new layouts); the undo history restarts.

reload.description: Map the new build after a successful build

tools.name: module_test
tools.description: Run the project's tests with ctest in the module's build tree (default filter: tests named <game>_*, such as the <game>_headless_300 smoke test). Returns each test's result and the output's end when one failed.

tools.name: test_run
tools.description: Run playtest scenarios without a person: .mctest files (JSON) under the project's tests/ folder, one file or folder ('path'), or one inline scenario ('test'). A scenario plays a saved scene headless with scripted input or a built-in bot, may stop early ('until'), and checks component fields (at the end or at a tick), entities alive, event counts, the log and the bot's feel metrics. Returns each scenario's checks with actual values, its state_hash, and the feel report (time to finish, deaths, stuck spots, idle time) when it has an actor.

path.description: A .mctest file or a folder of them inside the project (default tests/)

test.description: One scenario inline, in the .mctest format: {name, scene, ticks, input | bot, actor, until, death, assert: [checks], trace}

tools.name: playtest
tools.description: Let a built-in bot play the scene and say how it felt: walk_to (head for a point or entity, jumping or sidestepping when stuck), explore (seeded random wandering, coverage) or masher (random button chords, crash and soft-lock hunting). Returns the feel report: time to finish, deaths, stuck spots with positions, idle time, distance, cells visited. Needs no game code: the bot drives the game's input actions (Move, Jump, ...).

bot.description: {kind: walk_to|explore|masher, actor: entity, target: [x,y(,z)] or entity (walk_to), through: [waypoints, points or entities, reached in order before target] (walk_to), air_jumps: 0-4 extra Jump presses in the air (walk_to, side view), plane: xy|x|xz (default xy; x = side view with Jump, xz = 3D ground), reach: m (0.5), seed, move: action (Move), jump: action (Jump), actions: [names] (masher), period: ticks (8)}

scene.description: A saved scene under assets/ (default: the open scene)

until.description: Stop early when this check holds (a field, alive or event check)

death.description: Count a death each time this check becomes true, e.g. {entity, field: Health.hp, <=: 0}

trace.description: {every: ticks, fields: [{entity, field}]}: sample fields during the run

tools.name: docs_search
tools.description: Search the engine's shipped docs (user guide, engine reference), the worked samples and the example games. Returns the best sections with their mce://docs/... resource URI, heading, line and a snippet; read the whole file with resources/read. Start with mce://docs/index.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "camera shake" or "RigidBody2D"

tools.name: engine_capabilities
tools.description: What a game reaches through what: each engine feature with how it is reached today (data: a component; asset: a source file type; mcp: a tool; console; code: needs game C++), plus every component, importable asset type, tool and the convar count. Read this before planning a game, to keep game code to the rules.

area.description: Only this area's features (2D, 3D, physics, audio, input, ui, gameplay, scenes, agent, ...)

tools.name: gen_palette
tools.description: Generate a color palette (dark to light) from a seed and a scheme: analogous, complementary, triad, pastel, earth, neon or mono. Returns the colors as hex with a swatch image. 'save' writes it as a 1-pixel-high PNG strip under assets/.

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_sprite
tools.description: Generate pixel-art sprites: a mirrored, outlined, shaded creature, character, ship, item or blob from a seed, in 'colors' (hex, dark to light, at least 3; the darkest outlines) or a palette 'scheme'. 'variants' puts that many (seeds seed, seed+1, ...) in one row. Returns the frames' rects and an enlarged preview. 'save' writes the PNG under assets/ (nearest filtering, no mips) with its sidecar and a CREDITS.md row.

scheme.description: Palette scheme when 'colors' is not given (gen_palette's)

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_pixels
tools.description: Draw a pixel-art image from text: 'rows' is one string per pixel row (all the same length), 'palette' maps each character to a hex color ('.' and ' ' are transparent). For a specific shape (a moth, a lantern, a door) that gen_sprite's seeds will not give. Returns an enlarged preview; 'save' writes the PNG with its sidecar (nearest filtering) and a CREDITS.md row.

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_mesh
tools.description: Make a simple 3D mesh for blocking out a level or a toy-like game: a box, plane, sphere, cylinder, cone, disc or ramp (a wedge rising towards +X), centred on the origin with Y up, 'size' its full extent in metres, in one 'color' with 'roughness'. Returns its vertex and triangle counts and a shaded preview; 'save' writes it as a .glb (with its material inline) and a CREDITS.md row. Place it with the 3D kit's MeshRef (and MeshCollider3D).

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_tileset
tools.description: Generate a pixel-art tile set in one row: fill, fill_2, fill_3 (variations), top, top_left, top_right (surface edges), platform and decoration. Styles: grass, stone, brick, dirt, sand, snow, water, wood, metal. Returns each tile's rect and a preview; 'save' writes the PNG under assets/ for a TileMap's tile set.

colors.description: 4 fill colors dark to light, or 4 fill + 3 surface colors (default: the style's)

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_texture
tools.description: Generate a noise texture (value, perlin, fbm, ridged, worley; tileable by default) mapped through 'colors' gradient stops, or an equirect sky (kind sky: horizon, zenith and cloud colors, 'clouds' cover, 'stars' density; width = 2 x height) for a skybox or a backdrop. 'save' writes the PNG under assets/ (linear filtering, mips).

colors.description: Gradient stops low to high (sky: horizon, zenith, clouds)

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_sfx
tools.description: Generate a retro sound effect with an sfxr synthesizer: a preset (pickup, laser, explosion, powerup, hit, jump, blip, random) varied by the seed, with any sfxr parameter overridden in 'params'. Returns the parameters used (tweak and call again), the length and level, and a waveform image. 'save' writes a 16-bit WAV under assets/.

params.description: sfxr parameters to override, e.g. {"wave": "sine", "base_freq": 0.4, "env_decay": 0.3}; wave is square, saw, sine or noise; the result lists every parameter with its value

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_music
tools.description: Generate a seamless music loop (bass, chords, melody and optional drums) in a scale on a root note, exactly 'bars' bars of 4 beats at 'bpm', at most 60 seconds. Returns its length and a waveform image; 'save' writes a 16-bit WAV under assets/ (set the AudioSource to loop).

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: library_search
tools.description: Search the engine's bundled content library: CC0 models and sounds (Kenney), OFL and MIT fonts, and generator recipes (skies, textures, sprites, sounds, music). Every word must match an entry's id, title or tags. Returns ids for library_add, with license and author.

query.description: Words, e.g. "road corner" or "coin"; empty lists everything

tools.name: library_add
tools.description: Copy a library entry into the project's assets/ (its files, the files they need such as a model's texture, and a font's license text) with fresh .mceasset sidecars and a CREDITS.md row naming the author and license; a recipe runs its generator and saves the result. Default folder by kind: models/, sfx/, music/, fonts/, textures/.

path.description: A folder under assets/ ending in '/', or the main file's new path

tools.name: project_check
tools.description: Check the project before shipping and get findings to act on, each with severity, file, line, message and a fix: cook (assets and scenes that fail to import), references (GUIDs no asset has), unused (assets nothing references), credits (media files with no CREDITS.md row), srgb (data textures imported as sRGB, colour textures as linear), performance (each scene run headless: ms per tick against budget_ms) and accessibility (2D text height in pixels on a 1280x720 screen and its contrast against the background). pass is true when there is no error.

ticks.description: Ticks per scene for the performance check

budget_ms.description: Average sim milliseconds per tick allowed

tools.name: ship_build
tools.description: Make the release zip: the project's full CMake build (host, game module and the cooked pack; the module is mapped again), a smoke run of the host headless for 'ticks' ticks, then the SDK's `mce ship` (host, module, engine library, assets.mce, CREDITS.md). Returns each stage and the zip's path; ok is false with the stage that failed and the end of its output. Needs the server of an installed SDK (mce mcp <project>).

build.description: Run the full build first (false: ship what is built)

version.description: Version in the zip's name (default: the .mceproj's, else the SDK's)

out.description: Folder inside the project for the zip (default dist/)

tools.name: project_watch
tools.description: What the other agents on this project did: the event feed (.mce/events.jsonl), one event per write with agent, tool, path and time, numbered by seq. Pass the last call's next as since to get only new events; others: true leaves out your own. agent is your name (--agent, else the client's name and a suffix).

tools.name: asset_lock
tools.description: Lock a file under assets/ (a scene, prefab, material, texture...) so other agents' writes to it are refused until you unlock it or the lock's ttl runs out. Locking a file you hold refreshes it; an expired lock is taken over.

note.description: What you are doing, shown to the others

tools.name: asset_unlock
tools.description: Release a lock you hold. force: true breaks another agent's lock (the feed records it).

tools.name: asset_locks
tools.description: List the project's asset locks: path, agent, since, ttl, note and whether each expired.

tools.name: task_list
tools.description: The project's shared task list (tasks.mctasks): id, title, status (open, claimed, done, blocked), owner, notes, depends and files, with counts per status.

tools.name: task_add
tools.description: Add a task to the shared list. depends: ids of tasks that must be done before it can be claimed; files: the assets it will touch, so others know.

tools.name: task_claim
tools.description: Claim a task: it becomes yours (status claimed). Without id, the first open task whose dependencies are done. Two agents never get the same task.

tools.name: task_update
tools.description: Change a task's status (done, blocked, or open to give it back) and append a note signed with your name. Only the owner changes a claimed task's status.

tools.name: scene_switch
tools.description: Make another scene the open one, keeping the current one open in the background with its unsaved edits; switching back restores them. scene_save saves the current scene.

tools.name: scene_documents
tools.description: The scenes this server has open: the current one and the ones scene_switch parked, each with dirty.

tools.name: report_friction
tools.description: Write down something the engine made hard (a missing tool, a confusing error, a doc that was wrong, a workaround you had to invent) as a note in the project's friction.jsonl, so the engine's developers fix it. Call it when it happens, before working around it. blocking: you could not finish without a workaround.

area.description: The tool or engine area, e.g. render_frame, physics2d, docs

tool.description: The tool call that hit it

tools.name: asset_schema
tools.description: Describe a JSON source asset type: its fields (type, default, help) and the template asset_create starts from. Without 'type': the types asset_create/asset_write handle (.mcpart, .mcseq, .mctilemap, .mcsheet, .mcanim, .mcmat, .mcinput, .mcstore, .mcservices, .mcui, .mcconfig).

type.description: ParticlePreset, Sequence, Tilemap, SpriteSheet, AnimGraph, Material, InputMap, StoreCatalog, GameServicesCatalog, UiDocument, UiTheme, RemoteConfig, or the extension

tools.name: asset_create
tools.description: Create a JSON source asset at 'path' (its extension picks the type) with a fresh GUID: the type's template with 'content' fields over it. The document is cooked in memory first; a document the cook refuses is not written and the error names the field. A .mctilemap needs content.tileset ("guid:<Texture>"), columns and rows (the tileset's cells), width and height; its tiles start empty. Returns the path and "guid:<uuid>" to reference it.

path.description: New file under assets/, e.g. effects/dust.mcpart

tools.name: asset_write
tools.description: Change a JSON source asset (by path or guid), keeping its GUID. mode "merge" (default): 'content' fields replace the file's same-named fields, others stay; "replace": the document becomes exactly 'content'. Cooked in memory first: a refused document leaves the file unchanged.

tools.name: asset_read
tools.description: Read a JSON source asset (by path or guid): its path, guid, type and parsed content (scenes and prefabs too).

tools.name: tilemap_paint
tools.description: Paint a .mctilemap (by path or guid) in one call: 'clear' sets every tile first, then 'cells' [[x, y, tile]], 'rects' [[x0, y0, x1, y1, tile]] (inclusive, clipped) and 'fills' [[x, y, tile]] (flood fill of the region holding (x, y)) apply in that order. x right, y up, (0, 0) bottom-left; tile 0 erases, n draws tileset cell n-1. Every operation is checked before any applies. preview: true returns the map as text rows, top row first.

tools.name: prefab_create_from
tools.description: Save an entity and its ChildOf subtree as a new .mcprefab (fresh GUID; the root first, references that leave the subtree nulled) and cook it. replace (default true): the subtree becomes an instance of the new prefab at the same place, parent and transform, one undo step. Returns the prefab's "guid:<uuid>" and the instance id.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

path.description: New file under assets/, e.g. prefabs/enemy.mcprefab

tools.name: prefab_apply
tools.description: Write a prefab instance's overrides (of 'component', or of every overridden component except LocalTransform) into its .mcprefab root and re-cook it: every instance sees the values, and they stop being this instance's overrides. Entity references stay overrides.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: prefab_revert
tools.description: Drop a prefab instance's overrides (of 'component', or of every component except LocalTransform): the fields take the prefab's values again, and a component the prefab root lacks is removed.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: project_get
tools.description: The project's .mceproj (name, title, engine_version, games, plugins, start_scene as a GUID, with start_scene_path) and the open scene's WorldSettings (null when the scene has none).

tools.name: project_set
tools.description: Change .mceproj members: name, title, engine_version (strings), games, plugins (arrays of strings), start_scene (a scene's path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"). Checked before the file is written; other members are kept. A game's host reads start_scene when its build is configured: rebuild it to play the new one.

tools.name: scene_settings_get
tools.description: The open scene's WorldSettings (2D and 3D physics gravity), or null when it has none.

tools.name: scene_settings_set
tools.description: Change the open scene's WorldSettings fields (refl_describe_component WorldSettings lists them), e.g. {"gravity_2d": [0, -20]}; an entity "World Settings" carrying it is created when the scene has none. The stock player, run_headless and play-in-editor apply it at the first tick.

tools.name: ui_list
tools.description: UI documents (.mcui): without 'document', every one in the project with its widget count and the input actions its widgets raise; with 'document', its widgets in order as paths ("menu/play") with kind, text, action, bind and convar. A scene shows a document through a UiScreen component.

document.description: The UI document: a .mcui path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

tools.name: ui_create
tools.description: Make a new UI document (.mcui) with a fresh GUID: 'widgets' in the .mcui widget format (asset_schema type UiDocument describes it: name, kind, at | fill | anchors, style, styles, text, action, bind, format, children, ...). Checked by the cook before it is written; saved in the canonical form.

path.description: New .mcui path under assets/, e.g. ui/hud.mcui

modal.description: false: a HUD that never takes focus

tools.name: ui_widget_add
tools.description: Add a widget (with any children) to a UI document under 'parent' (a widget path; omitted: the root), last or at 'index' among the siblings. 'widget' is a .mcui widget object; it starts from the look its kind gets in code. Nav paths in it are paths from the document root.

document.description: The UI document: a .mcui path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

parent.description: Parent widget path, e.g. menu; omitted: the root

widget.description: A .mcui widget: {name, kind, text, at, style, action, bind, children, ...}

index.description: Position among the parent's children (default last)

tools.name: ui_widget_set
tools.description: Change a widget of a UI document: 'fields' are .mcui widget keys that replace the widget's own (null removes one, e.g. "action": null). "style" changes the listed UiStyle fields in every state, "styles": {"Hover": {...}} in one state, "nav" the listed edges; one of at / fill / anchors replaces the anchors. Renaming with "name" breaks nav paths that name the old path (the call then fails).

document.description: The UI document: a .mcui path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

tools.name: ui_widget_remove
tools.description: Remove a widget and its children from a UI document. Fails when another widget's nav still names it.

document.description: The UI document: a .mcui path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

tools.name: ui_preview
tools.description: See a UI document alone: the real player draws it over a plain background at a viewport size, safe area and UI scale, and the frame comes back as a PNG (offscreen software rendering when there is no display). Bound fields read the open (saved) scene, else the project's first scene. 'save' also writes the PNG for image_diff.

document.description: The UI document: a .mcui path under assets/ or "guid:<uuid>"

safe_area.description: Insets in pixels {left, top, right, bottom}: the UI lays out inside them; the image outlines them

save.description: Also write the PNG inside the project folder, e.g. shots/hud.png
